lines.text: In the old Norse tales, a serpent grew so vast it wrapped around the whole world and bit its own tail — an unbroken circle nothing could break. That is Jormungandr, the World Serpent.
And tonight, out of the shadow, come the Three Lions of England — a nation that has chased one more great night for longer than it cares to remember.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends. Norway, versus England. A play-off. Two forces locked together, and neither one willing to yield an inch.
Norway arrive with a generation of giants and nothing to fear. England arrive as the heavyweights, carrying every expectation in the game.
Norway — the sons of the fjords, built around raw northern power and one of the most frightening front lines football has right now.
Erling Haaland, number nine — a pure force of nature.
Martin Odegaard, the captain, number ten — the mind of this team.
Alexander Sorloth, number eleven — the second tower, all power.
Antonio Nusa, number twenty — the young spark, fearless and direct.
And Sander Berge, number six — tall, calm, in control of midfield.
England — the Three Lions, the nation of endless expectation, desperate to finally turn all that talent into one unforgettable night.
Harry Kane, the captain, number nine — the complete, deadly striker.
Jude Bellingham, number ten — all drive and swagger.
Declan Rice, number four — the engine of this whole team.
Bukayo Saka, number seven — electric feet, cutting inside to shoot.
And around them, the Three Lions — pace, power and depth.
So here is the riddle. When two forces are this evenly matched, what happens when neither one is willing to break?
And stay with me — because tonight turns on a name from Norse legend that has waited a thousand years to be told.
Here's how we see it — England start on top, sharp and confident, hunting the first blow.
England build with menace, the heavyweights probing, looking for the crack to strike through first.
And Kane strikes! The captain finds a yard in the box in the first half, and England lead one to nothing.
Now the coil tightens around them — England in front, but Norway rising, and Haaland smelling blood.
And here come the Norwegians. Wave after wave from the fjords, the giants throwing everything at the English wall.
And Haaland answers! One flash of that terrifying power, and Norway are level — one to one, the circle closes.
Now neither side will yield. England surge back, Kane and Bellingham hunting the goal that would break the deadlock.
Norway hit straight back. Haaland and Sorloth rising together, England holding on at the very edge of the storm.
Blow for blow, end to end, and every time one side pushes, the other refuses to fall. The serpent's coil will not break.
Still they trade. Still it holds. Two great forces locked together, and not a single inch given by either one.
And the final whistle! One to one — honours even, a night where neither side would yield, and neither side deserved to lose.
One to one. England struck first, Norway struck back, and the circle held to the very last breath.
England could not put the giants away. Norway stared down the heavyweights and never blinked.
Two teams, level and unbroken. Some of the greatest nights are the ones nobody wins.
Our prediction — Norway one, England one. Kane, then Haaland. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
So you tell me — did Norway earn the point of their lives, or did England let this one slip? Comment NORWAY for the fjords — comment ENGLAND for the Three Lions.
They say the World Serpent and the thunder god will meet at the end of days, and strike each other down together — the ultimate draw, two powers so equal that neither can survive the other.
The players write tonight's story. But Jormungandr carries one truth — when two forces are perfectly equal, the circle will not break.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and Jormungandr, Legend one-zero-three, is yours.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for glory.
